evals.prompt: A frozen design requires one bounded agent to choose diagnostic read tools from observations. We need two approved model providers and application-owned state. Select a minimal general agent stack; no framework is fixed.
evals.expected_output: Prefer OpenAI Agents SDK while qualifying each provider route and retaining application controls.
assertions: Selects OpenAI Agents SDK as the preferred general kernel without requiring OpenAI models.
Keeps one bounded agent and avoids mandatory gateway, vector store or workflow engine.
Qualifies tool, structured-output, stream and data-policy support for each exact route.
Distinguishes documented SDK support from measured target readiness.

evals.prompt: Our approved architecture explicitly fixes Pydantic AI for a bounded agent. Review its model-access, tools and durable-state boundaries; do not migrate frameworks.
evals.expected_output: Honor the explicit Pydantic AI decision and review only undecided boundaries.
assertions: Preserves the explicitly fixed Pydantic AI framework.
Does not wrap OpenAI Agents SDK inside Pydantic AI or recommend an unsolicited migration.
Retains application-owned authorization, state, budgets and provider qualification.

evals.prompt: Select a stack for one structured extraction model call followed by validation and saving. Code decides every transition. The existing provider task API supplies the required schema.
evals.expected_output: Use a direct call with deterministic processing and no agent kernel.
assertions: Classifies the model operation as direct-call behavior and continuation as code-owned.
Does not introduce Agents SDK, Pydantic AI Agent, multi-agent topology or a graph merely for consistency.
Keeps saving behind deterministic validation and effect authority.

evals.prompt: A frozen agent design requires strict schemas on a mandatory provider. Controlled tests prove that neither the preferred SDK built-in route nor its qualified adapters can deliver that capability. No alternate framework has been authorized. Give the stack decision.
evals.expected_output: Report the preferred-SDK gate as blocked and offer an explicit override decision.
assertions: Does not claim compatibility or waive the schema requirement.
Does not silently select another general kernel.
Explains the evidence gap or failure, identifies a viable alternative for explicit override, and preserves the frozen behavior contract.

evals.prompt: Review a proposed Agents SDK service: every tenant shares a mutable default client; it replays SDK history and provider conversation state together, trusts restored approvals, treats cancelled streams as stopped tools, and exports all traces by default.
evals.expected_output: Identify concrete authority, state, concurrency, cleanup and privacy defects.
assertions: Scopes identity-bearing clients and route configuration per admitted run or tenant.
Selects one coherent history owner and revalidates approvals against current authority.
Separates stream termination from remote quiescence and retains unknown effects.
Sets approved trace export and retention before execution.

evals.prompt: An existing app uses direct calls. We now need a general agent that calls a coding specialist for repository analysis. Select the agent runtime and specialist boundary without requiring a hosted provider or new infrastructure.
evals.expected_output: Prefer Agents SDK for the general agent and a scoped Codex coding specialist when its harness is justified.
assertions: Separates general-agent kernel from coding-harness selection.
Keeps specialist context, tools, authority and budget bounded.
Does not infer deep app-server integration or distributed infrastructure from a specialist requirement.
